correctness.rationale: The connected incidence graph has a unique bipartition up to reversal. Its part-preserving maps are the 168 invertible linear maps: images of a noncollinear basis triple determine the collineation by the Fano lines {u,v,u+v}. Dot-product polarity supplies the other coset. In the barycentric subdivision the strictly increasing face sizes prohibit inversions, and every orbit of open simplices is an open cell of the ordinary quotient. Orientation by inclusion order yields the signed orbit-of-deletion boundary and the corresponding triangular attaching words, with no multiplicity from stabilizers. Finite dimensional exhaustion follows also from the linear incidence equations: one point allows four nonincident lines, a pair allows two, and a triple allows at most one, with the dual bounds for lines. Thus mixed faces have size at most five and pure faces at most seven. An independent Python standard-library enumeration, using line normals and integer Smith operations, reproduced 457 nonempty faces, 336 automorphisms, orbit cell counts (14,64,149,218,210,120,30), boundary ranks (13,51,98,120,90,30), and only unit nonzero Smith factors. Boundary compositions were zero. Primitivity means each image is saturated in the ambient free chain group, hence also in the kernel of the preceding boundary; rank differences then give integral acyclicity, not just rational acyclicity. The independent triangular presentation has a 13-edge spanning tree, 51 generators and 149 relators. Unit eliminations killed all 51, leaving only empty words, so the quotient is simply connected. Hurewicz at a least possible nonzero homotopy degree and Whitehead give contractibility of this finite CW complex.
residual_risks: This is exhaustive for the given graph and action, not for subgroups, other graphs or homotopy quotients. The two relator slots remaining in the independent run are empty words.

evidence: The ambient wedge of six 3-spheres is simply connected. The rational collineation representation has no invariant vector, so the full quotient has no positive rational homology: for finite actions the barycentric orbit chains over Q are coinvariants and coinvariants are exact.

By the standard orbit fundamental group theorem for a finite action on a simply connected polyhedron, fixed-point elements normally generate the kernel from the action group. Elementary transvections generate GL(3,2) and fix points of the Fano plane; dot-product polarity fixes the midpoint of the independent pair consisting of (1,0,0) and its polar line. Thus trivial quotient fundamental group is already a consequence of the ambient result with this standard argument.
Neither argument gives the saturated integral boundary images verified here. Rational acyclicity plus simple connectivity by itself leaves possible higher-degree integral torsion.

value.rationale: The ordinary symmetry quotient of the canonical Fano-plane independence complex is a natural exact invariant. Establishing that it has no integral obstruction, in contrast to what the ambient type and rational representation could decide alone, answers a concrete topological question about retaining full duality. The distinction is relevant to other geometric independence quotients, where positive-degree torsion can survive. The value is the complete answer for this natural object, not the size of the enumeration or a general family claim.
residual_risks: The value judgment does not rely on novelty of the fundamental group or on generalization to proper subgroups or higher-order planes.
